kurz: Why the name does not matter when choosing among thousands of listed products, and in which order the index, the tax wrapper and the costs are checked.

bloecke.md:
On 8 September 2026, around 2,970 ETFs were listed on Deutsche Börse, plus 205 ETCs and 361 ETNs. The three abbreviations denote different products. An ETF is a fund whose assets are kept separate from the assets of the management company (for German funds, these are [[Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)|segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)]]). An ETC or ETN is a debt security that carries the default risk of the issuer. An investor who buys a gold ETC because the search screen shows it next to the equity ETFs has thereby already made the first selection decision without noticing.

The selection itself consists of two decisions of very different weight. The first concerns the index, that is, the markets, countries and company sizes in which the fund invests. It determines almost the entire return. The second concerns the wrapper, that is, the question of which provider tracks this index in which legal form, with which domicile and at what ongoing costs. It accounts for only tenths of a percentage point. In practice, the second decision usually receives more attention than the first.

bloecke.unter: At the top are the criteria that determine the return, at the bottom those that shift it only by fractions. Public discussion usually starts with the lower ones.

stufen.text: Markets, countries, size classes. Explains almost the entire return.
Fund domicile, partial exemption (Teilfreistellung), distribution policy. Small but permanent amounts.
Tracking difference ahead of TER, spread, savings plan fee
Fund size, age, provider, savings plan availability at your own broker

bloecke.md:
## Choosing the index (step 1)

The range on offer is dominated by three indices that are not interchangeable. The MSCI World contains 23 developed markets and around 1,250 stocks, but neither emerging markets nor small caps. According to the MSCI factsheet, its US share was 72.1% as of 31 August 2026. The MSCI ACWI adds the emerging markets and comes to 47 countries and around 2,410 stocks, with an emerging markets share of about 12%. The FTSE All-World covers 49 countries and around 4,200 stocks, with about 10% in emerging markets.

The fact that FTSE shows fewer emerging markets than MSCI is due to a different country classification. FTSE lists South Korea as a developed market, MSCI as an emerging market. The higher number of stocks results from broader coverage, because FTSE covers around 90% of market capitalisation and MSCI around 85%. To cover small companies as well, an index with the abbreviation IMI or All-Cap is needed. At the end of August 2026, the MSCI ACWI IMI comprised 8,162 stocks; according to the provider, the SPDR MSCI ACWI IMI held 5,998 stocks. There is also a third index family. The Amundi Prime All Country World tracks a Solactive GBS index and, with ongoing charges of 0.07%, is the cheapest broad world ETF. In return, you follow a different index provider with its own methodology and a shorter history.

bloecke.unter: Share of US equities in three broad world ETFs as a percentage, data from justETF, as of 31 August 2026. The highest and the lowest US share differ by around ten percentage points, and this difference weighs more heavily than any question of cost.

bloecke.titel: Large world ETFs compared, as of July to September 2026

bloecke.md: All eight funds are domiciled in Ireland. The size column is where the comparison portals most often differ from one another. The two Vanguard rows are two share classes of the same fund. As of 31 July 2026, the distributing class reported around $26.2 billion, and the fund as a whole, across all classes, around $79.6 billion. Both figures are correct; they refer to different things. Whether a product is large enough is measured by the fund as a whole rather than by the individual class. Each of these figures also comes with a reference date.

## Costs beyond the TER (step 2)

The total expense ratio (TER) states the published ongoing costs. The [[Tracking difference|tracking difference]], by contrast, measures how far the fund return lagged behind the index return. It also includes transaction costs, sampling deviations, withholding tax effects and income from securities lending. For the iShares Core MSCI World, it has averaged around 0.03% a year since 2010, although the TER is 0.20%. Comparing two ETFs on the TER alone can therefore lead to the wrong result.

The Irish domicile has a tax reason. The double taxation agreement between Ireland and the US reduces US withholding tax on dividends to 15%, while Luxembourg physical funds in practice often bear the full 30%. With a US dividend yield of 1.6%, around 0.24 versus 0.48 percentage points of return a year are lost as a result before they reach the fund assets. The domicile is shown in the first two characters of the ISIN (IE or LU).

The second tax question can only be clarified with the prospectus; the product name says nothing about it. For tax withholding by the bank, the 30% [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption]] for equity funds under Section 20 InvStG (Investment Tax Act) requires the investment conditions (Anlagebedingungen) to commit to investing more than 50% in equity participations on a continuous basis (Section 2(6) InvStG). For the tax withholding, only this commitment counts. An ETF that in fact holds only shares but does not commit itself in its investment conditions receives 0% in the tax withholding. The partial exemption can then only be claimed in the tax return, with proof that the fund exceeded the ratio continuously throughout the calendar year (Section 20(4) InvStG).

With a price gain of €10,000 and the saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag) used up, €7,000 is taxable with the partial exemption. At 26.375% including solidarity surcharge, this gives €1,846 of flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer); without the partial exemption, it is €2,638. In practice, individual swap and specialised structures are affected. The key information document contains no information on this, but the prospectus does.

## Fund size and age (step 3)

Below a fund size of about €50 million to €100 million, running an ETF hardly pays for itself. From around €100 million, the industry regards a product as cost-efficient and at low risk of closure. Age is the second filter criterion. For a fund with a twelve-month history, no reliable tracking difference can be determined; that requires at least three to five years.

A large fund size, on the other hand, does not guarantee narrow spreads. The spread depends on the liquidity of the shares held and on the number of market makers, not on the size of the fund. For the two most actively traded world ETFs, the Xetra Liquidity Measure (XLM), which states what an immediate purchase and sale of €100,000 costs as a result of the spread and market depth, stood at around 2 basis points in September 2026; outside core trading hours, spreads are considerably wider. Before 15:30, the US shares in the fund are also valued only at estimated prices.

bloecke.titel: Types of cost for a small and a large portfolio
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation in euros a year with a monthly instalment of €300 (€3,600 a year). The first series shows the first year with an average portfolio value of €1,950, built up linearly with no return assumed; the second shows the same savings plan at a portfolio value of €100,000. A half spread of two basis points is incurred on each of the twelve purchases.

bloecke.md: Savings plan availability therefore belongs on the list of criteria just as much as the TER, but its weight decreases rather than increases as the portfolio grows. With a monthly instalment of €300, an execution fee of 1.75% costs €63 a year. A TER of 0.20% only reaches the same €63 at a portfolio value of €31,500. In the first years, it is therefore the broker that determines the costs, and later the product. A TER difference of 0.13 percentage points amounts to €130 a year on €100,000, permanently and without any action by the investor. A free savings plan is co-financed by the provider's other revenue. Inducements from trading venues or market makers for routing orders have been banned since 1 July 2026. Fee-free promotional lists also come to an end without the savings plan stopping as a result.

- An ETF can be closed. According to industry counts, around 230 ETFs were liquidated in the US in 2025; in Europe, liquidations are considerably rarer but do occur. Signs of this are a small fund size, low trading volume and many competing products on the same index.
- For niche and thematic products, there are figures from Morningstar (observation period ending mid-2024). Of the thematic funds, 94% survived the first year; after ten years, three in four were still in existence, and after fifteen years, 45%.
- The label and the index can change. Since September 2022, around 307 funds with about €175 billion have downgraded their SFDR status from Article 9 to Article 8. The ISIN and name stay the same while the content changes.
- In a merger, the fund is absorbed into another fund. The tax consequences are set out in the investor information on the merger and should be read there.

A holding is worth €20,000, of which €8,000 is unrealised gain. The saver's allowance of €1,000 is still unused. If the fund is liquidated, it is settled at net asset value. This amounts to a sale that the investor did not choose.

After the 30% partial exemption, €5,600 is taxable, or €4,600 after deducting the allowance. At 26.375%, this gives €1,213 in tax that would otherwise have stayed in the portfolio. Calculated over a further fifteen years at 6%, the portfolio is around €2,910 smaller at the end. Without the liquidation, the tax on the gain to date would be due on the sale after these fifteen years, so the disadvantage after tax is around €1,100 (illustrative calculation). The disadvantage arises from the forced timing of taxation rather than from the fund itself. This is why fund size is also a tax criterion for selection.

schritte.text: First, decide whether developed markets, the whole world or the whole world including small caps should be covered. The decision is made before any product search and is recorded in writing.
Exact index name, fund size above €100 million, launched at least three years ago, Irish domicile for US-heavy indices.
Set the values for three to five years side by side instead of sorting by TER. Without a history, no judgement is possible.
Replication method, extent of securities lending according to the annual report, distribution policy and the equity ratio committed to in the prospectus.
Clarify whether the ETF is available as a savings plan there, what execution costs and whether the ETF can be traded on a trading venue with continuous pricing.
Buy with a limit order during core trading hours and then check the factsheet once a year. Switching without a reason costs tax on the gain to date.

bloecke.titel: Where to find the fund information
bloecke.md:
- The key information document (at most three pages, required by law) states the ongoing charges, the risk indicator and the investment objective.
- The prospectus and investment conditions contain the ratio commitment on which the partial exemption depends.
- The annual report shows the extent, income and collateralisation of securities lending.
- The provider's factsheet gives the country and sector weights, the number of stocks and the exact wording of the index name.
- Comparison portals are suitable for tracking difference and fund size; always read the reference date and the scope of the figures as well.

The index determines the return, the wrapper accounts for tenths of a percentage point, and the broker determines the costs of the first years. If you check these three levels in this order, you will arrive at a sound result with any of the large world ETFs, even though none of them is perfect.

mitnehmen: The choice of index (developed markets or the whole world, with or without small caps) determines the return; all further decisions shift it only by fractions.

For comparison purposes, what counts is the tracking difference over several years rather than the TER; for the iShares Core MSCI World, it has averaged around 0.03% since 2010, against a TER of 0.20%.
Fund size and age are criteria for a fund's survival, because below about €100 million the risk of closure rises, and a liquidation forces a taxable sale at net asset value.

The domicile can be recognised from the ISIN, and for tax withholding the partial exemption depends on the ratio commitment in the investment conditions (Section 2(6), Section 20 InvStG); the composition of the portfolio counts only if it is proven in the tax return (Section 20(4) InvStG).
In the first years of saving, the execution fee costs more than the fund costs; with a monthly instalment of €300, the relationship reverses from a portfolio value of around €31,500.

begriffe.text: Country in which the fund is established, recognisable from the first two characters of the ISIN (IE = Ireland, LU = Luxembourg). It determines the applicable double taxation agreement and thus the non-refundable withholding tax on dividends in the fund assets.

One of several tranches of the same fund, for example an accumulating one and a distributing one, with its own ISIN but shared fund assets. This explains why portals give very different sizes for the same product.

Flat-rate compensation for the tax already borne at fund level. For an equity fund held as private assets, 30% of the income remains tax-free (Section 20 InvStG). The condition is that the investment conditions commit to more than 50% equity participations on a continuous basis (Section 2(6) InvStG), or that the investor proves in the tax return that the fund exceeded this ratio continuously throughout the calendar year (Section 20(4) InvStG).

Liquidation of a fund by the management company. The units are settled at net asset value, and the gain accumulated up to that point is realised and taxed compulsorily, regardless of whether the timing suits the investor.

Exchange-traded commodity, that is, an exchange-traded debt security on a commodity. It is usually collateralised but does not constitute segregated fund assets. Although it is traded in a similar way to an ETF, the buyer bears the issuer's default risk.
